indicators.note: the word for strategy holds the next piece within it

parts.note: a strategy is a plan

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of Iran

explanation.surface: A clear-cut policy that, at its start, involves Iran.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contains' puts I, the first letter of Iran, inside PLAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Clear in the sense of obvious or unadorned is a synonym.

indicators.note: catching means the word for law grabs and holds the politician inside it

parts.note: a law is a rule
MP, Member of Parliament, is the standard crossword politician

explanation.surface: Unrest arising when the law nabs a politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catching' is the container signal. Disorder is a verb here, to crumple or make untidy, not the noun it first appears to be.
explanation.definitionFit: To disorder hair or clothes is to tousle or crumple them, a synonym as a verb.

definitions.meaning: the valve or pedal controlling an engine's fuel flow and speed
to strangle someone by the throat

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses look automotive (a car also has a choke), but the second is strangling.
explanation.definitionFit: One word names both the engine's speed control and the act of strangling.

parts.note: a lei is a Hawaiian flower garland
guaranteed means certain, sure

explanation.surface: A holiday where you are certain to be given a flower garland.
explanation.definitionFit: Holiday and free time are close synonyms: time off work for rest.

indicators.note: the letters, or characters, of the two quoted words are formed again in a new order

explanation.surface: Conservatives declaring themselves virtuous by embracing former villains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reformed characters' is the anagram signal on the letters of TORIES HUG; the surface reads it as people who have mended their ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Good in the moral sense is a synonym of virtuous and upright.

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of socialist

parts.note: glee is merriment, laughter

explanation.surface: A left-wing chief gleefully crushing opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: To destroy utterly, especially to kill in great numbers or defeat heavily, is a synonym.

indicators.note: eating means the word for put off takes the next letter inside it

parts.note: to put off in nautical terms is to set sail from shore

explanation.surface: Someone deterred from a meal by being served a fresh slug-like creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put off' looks like 'deterred', but it is the sailor's sense, to set out from shore. 'eating' puts N inside SAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A gastropod with a coiled shell is an example of a mollusc.

indicators.note: changing tells us the letters of the car make are rearranged

explanation.surface: A French car shifting gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' signals the anagram of RENAULT; the question mark admits that this is one example of a gear position.
explanation.definitionFit: The position in which no gear is engaged is an example of a gear setting.

indicators.note: embracing means the outer letters hug the inner piece

parts.note: One's is I plus S, as in I is, one is
BI, short for bisexual, stands loosely for androgynous

explanation.surface: A self-description of someone holding an ambiguous-looking bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embracing' is the container signal. One's is read as 'one is', giving I and S; BI is a loose stand-in for androgynous.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-billed wading bird sacred in ancient Egypt is an example of a bird.

indicators.note: refining processes the drug, so its letters along with is are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A moral verdict on processing drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refining' signals the anagram of OPIUM IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking reverence, wicked; close enough to immoral in common usage.

clue.text: Got purchase from branch before top of tree

parts.note: a bough is a tree branch

indicators.note: the top of a down-reading word is its first letter, here of tree

explanation.surface: Someone getting a grip on a branch near the treetop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got purchase' reads as 'got a grip' when climbing, but it means acquired by buying.
explanation.definitionFit: Acquiring something by paying for it is the past tense of to buy.

clue.text: The French on street, just in case

parts.note: le is French for the

explanation.surface: A French phrase book's line for a street, kept for emergencies.
explanation.definitionFit: A conjunction meaning for fear that or so as to avoid; same sense as just in case.

definitions.meaning: held back or set aside for someone, as a table at a restaurant

explanation.walkthrough: The two words read together as 'kept silent', but each is a separate sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Booked in advance, and also reticent or restrained in character.

indicators.note: changing tells us the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A senator who is switching careers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' signals the anagram of SENATOR IS. 'profession' looks like a career, but it means a declaration, as in a profession of faith.
explanation.definitionFit: A profession is an open declaration or claim, the same as a statement of belief.

parts.note: bogus means fake, a sham
ED, short for editor, is the crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A fake reporter disgraced.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling disgraced and embarrassed: a synonym of humiliated.

indicators.note: in means Britain's letter sits inside the word for helping

parts.note: helping means aiding

explanation.surface: Britain lending a hand while keeping its status.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts B inside AIDING. 'standing' is an adjective: lasting, permanent.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasting or enduring, as a standing rule or an enduring love; a synonym as an adjective.

clue.text: Ring the telegraph perhaps, about nothing hard

indicators.note: about means the call phrase wraps around the zero

parts.note: an instruction to phone the newspaper itself: call us
O, the zero shape, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A reader told to phone the newspaper over a hard-hearted trifle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring the telegraph' looks like old telegraphy, but it is the newspaper speaking: call us. 'about' puts O inside CALLUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard-hearted and unfeeling; hard in the emotional sense is a synonym.

indicators.note: off signals the letters of the two words are taken out of order

explanation.surface: A gardener's order to deadhead a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' signals the anagram of LOP HEADS, while the surface makes it lopping the flower heads off.
explanation.definitionFit: A lily of the Mediterranean, the flower of the Greek underworld, is an example of a plant.

definitions.meaning: a framework of parallel or crossed bars, as over a drain
irritating, like a harsh scraping sound

explanation.definitionFit: A metal latticework over an opening, and an adjective for something irritating or harsh.

parts.note: re means about or concerning
the gist is the essential meaning
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword queen, placed by the rest

explanation.surface: Notes made about what a monarch meant.
explanation.definitionFit: An official list or log, such as a school's attendance list, is a record.

indicators.note: after tells us the letter for right comes second, following the word for match

parts.note: a tie is a match or fixture in sport, as in a cup tie

explanation.surface: A quarrel that broke out straight after a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests a quarrel, but it means a line of seats; 'after' sends R behind TIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A row of seats one above another is a level or layer, a synonym.

parts.note: to pip is to beat narrowly, pip at the post

explanation.surface: An English team just beaten on the Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' places E after PIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A tube carrying water or gas is a channel or conduit.

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held: 'River survey missing gold (6)'. Wordplay PANORAMA less OR gives the letters, but no well-known river bears that name, so 'River' does not define the answer; a hat or canal word may be missing.

indicators.note: housing means the run of letters sits inside these words, as a stable houses a horse

explanation.surface: A stable that may well shelter a creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'housing' signals the letters run across the end of 'Maybe', the word 'a' and the start of 'stable'.
explanation.definitionFit: A creature, especially a large four-footed one, is a synonym of animal.

indicators.note: on in an across clue means placed after the other piece

parts.note: tripe is nonsense, rubbish

explanation.surface: A pub serving rubbish food on Sundays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar's' looks like a pub owning something; the 's is a link. 'on' puts TRIPE after S.
explanation.definitionFit: A band or line of colour, as on a flag, is a bar.

indicators.note: the extremities of tender are its first and last letters

parts.note: an ounce is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A pound weight dropped on tender toes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' looks like the unit, in a clue full of weights, but it is the verb to batter.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat heavily or thrash; to pound an opponent is a synonym.

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
a go is an attempt, a try

explanation.surface: A professional giving up after an attempt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drop' looks like a fall, but it is the verb to give something up; 'by' simply sets the attempt beside the word for pro.
explanation.definitionFit: To give up or do without something is to drop it.

indicators.note: injured means the letters of the two words are hurt into a different order

explanation.surface: Trapped colliers who came out unhurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'injured' signals the anagram of MINERS NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Deepest inside, hidden at the core, as buried feelings are.
